note.p: There seem to be many contacts with Holm, and little reason to think that H Holm is used to distinguish two Holms. There is also one entry for H H Holm, which, again, does not seem to distinguish the individual from the other Holms. But there are instances where he says 2 Holm and 3 Holms, and one occasion on which he refers to Holm Senior, so there is a larger family.

There is a paper on Contributions to Pathologial Phrenology written by H H Holm in the London Medical and Physical Journal for 1833, Vol 14 (81) pp. 195-7. On the three occasions Holm is with Godwin when goes to an event given by the phrenologist Spuzheim; and he accompanies Godwin to King's College on one occasion. In the article, Holm is described as Lecturer in Phrenology in the School of Medicine, London Hospital (Whitechapel).

Henry Haley Holm was prosecuted and fined for a 'misdemeanour', for taking a head (that of his mother) from a vault in St Mary's Church, Hendon, in 1828. He explained that he sought to identify from the skull the marks of the family history of psychological illness. His father, John Diderick Holm (c1775-1856), was from Sweden, and was also a passionate phrenologoist and friend of Spurzheim. H Holm was a fellow of the Zoological Society, and a Member of the Royal College of Surgeons.
There are a great many individual calls back and forth, but Holm is also met regularly at Mrs Woods, and also at Martins , Sass's and L. Stanhope and has connections with Mary Shelley.
Holm married Eliza Cooke in April 1843, but died in March 1846. His residence is described as Mill Hill, Middlesex.
We are currently treating all the Holms as one Holm! The pattern of visits is odd, with frequent interaction and then periods in which Holm seems to be away.
There is also an odd document (C13/653/22 National Archive) suggesting a law suit with Hannah Haley and Henry Haley Holm as defendants, against John Diderrick Holm as plaintiff, dated 1810.
